extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers and scientific/medical professionals (readers of a popular science monthly)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative standards used in book reviews of scientific, medical, and popular-science works — covering usefulness, scope, scholarship, presentation, experimental evidence, and practical applicability. Focused on assessing books and reports for a general-educated/scientific readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness to intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Books should be welcomed for addressing important subjects and meet the needs of their intended audience (e.g., an 'American Health Primer' that teaches the public about the skin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value is placed on whether a work supplies necessary instruction for lay readers or specialists; repetition and clear inculcation may be required for public-health topics. Example: the primer is 'to be welcomed' because the skin is important and few are aware of it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of technical terms and popular nomenclature; thorough index
rubrics_metrics.description: Include medical/technical terms along with the popular names (both correctly and wrongly applied) and provide a particularly full index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer recommends consulting the index first; a full index and explicit treatment of nomenclature increases the book's practical value (author's prefatory note: 'it will be well first to consult the index, which has been made particularly full').

rubrics_metrics.name: Up-to-dateness and engagement with recent original research
rubrics_metrics.description: Textbooks should be written from the point of view of the latest original memoirs and continually refer to recent investigations rather than only to older texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A work that systematically incorporates and cites current experimental research is judged superior and better suited to students and practitioners (example: Gamgee's physiological chemistry is praised for this quality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation to appropriate disciplinary viewpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: The book's organizing perspective should fit its audience (e.g., treat physiological chemistry from the biologist/physician viewpoint rather than the chemist's).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviation from the 'typical plan' of other fields is acceptable when it better serves the target readership; reviewers note and evaluate this choice of standpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and independence as a textbook
rubrics_metrics.description: A volume should form a complete and independent work in its domain, even if further volumes are planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks are praised when they can be safely consulted on their own and when they comprehensively cover the stated subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental emphasis with appropriate mathematical rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Works on experimental sciences should emphasize experimental methods and limit mathematical formalism to what's necessary for the audience (e.g., limiting math to simple algebraic operations with supplementary appendices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers value an experimental approach accessible to non-mathematicians while providing appendices or footnotes for the more technical mathematics when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and usefulness of illustrations and engravings
rubrics_metrics.description: Books should be well illustrated with finely executed engravings representing apparatus and processes when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abundant, high-quality illustrations aid comprehension of experimental apparatus and methods and make the work valuable beyond specialists ('profusely illustrated with finely executed engravings').

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and concise exposition plus coverage of recent research
rubrics_metrics.description: Present main facts clearly and concisely while also exposing many of the more recent and important experimental researches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A balance of concise statement-of-facts and exposition of contemporary experiments is desirable; both accessibility and currency matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between theoretical exposition and practical/experimental detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Theoretical topics (e.g., Maxwell's electromagnetic theory) should be presented to the extent appropriate; reviewers may expect fuller exposition if the theory is central.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an author aims to interpret phenomena according to a particular theory, the reviewer assesses whether the theoretical treatment is sufficiently developed (critic: 'The theory might well bear a fuller exposition').

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate scope and depth for the format and price
rubrics_metrics.description: The ambition of the subject matter must match the length, format, and price of the book; large topics should not be 'dispatched' in too short a primer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism when two large topics are jammed into a fifty-cent primer: either allocate more space or split into separate books ('these topics are too large... to be both dispatched in a fifty-cent primer').

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical guidance and actionable content for activity-specific handbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Handbooks (e.g., for sea-voyages) should give specific, practical instructions about outfit, accommodations, expected conditions, routes, and management of health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value is placed on usable, portable advice that travelers can consult before and during voyages; reviewers highlight chapters of practical use and portability ('well worth consulting before going to sea, and... profitable to take it along').

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of authorities and handling of divergent opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: When authoritative sources differ, the author should cite recognized authorities and indicate the preponderant opinion or give reasons for a differing recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pronunciation manual is praised for citing recognized authorities and explaining when it prefers a different pronunciation ('recognized authorities are cited... when they differ the preponderant opinion is indicated').

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and direct practicality for emergency manuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency manuals should be brief but well-digested, pointed, and practical, providing immediate usable directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise, practical guidance is valued over length in life-saving contexts ('brief but well-digested... pointed and practical').

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical performance metrics and independent verification for technical apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims about performance (e.g., light output per horse-power) should be supported by experimental trials and independent testimony (e.g., Professor Morton's measurements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for empirical data on efficiency, power expenditure, and other measurable outcomes and cite test results when available to assess claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of practical drawbacks, maintenance, and long-term behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider potential disadvantages in practice (e.g., gasoline vapor depositing a film on glass, perceptible vibration of light) and the likelihood of maintenance issues over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even promising inventions are judged by foreseeable long-term practical problems and maintenance burdens; reviewers raise skeptical caveats drawn from early observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability and sensitivity of control/regulating mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulating devices should be tested for reliability and sensitivity (e.g., automatic current regulation that maintains steady light across varying circuit loads).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of delicate, certain action in regulators that prevents observable differences across a range of loads is an important performance criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and urgency of primary data collection in field sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Anthropological and ethnological work must gather and preserve facts promptly, before traditions and informants are lost; field travel and gaining trust are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer emphasizes the need for ethnologists to travel and collect documents now, warning 'every gap thus permitted will be painfully regretted' and noting the difficulty of accessing priestly/secret traditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough, detailed behavioral observation and avoidance of bias in animal studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal behavioral studies should record detailed habits and development, use concrete illustrative examples, and compare carefully to human behavior without overgeneralizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long descriptive anecdotes (e.g., of an ape's actions) are used to support judgments about faculties like reflection and comparison; reviewers value close observation and restraint in interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production and bibliographic details as indicators of value (price, pages, illustrations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical production details — page count, presence of illustrations, and price — are reported and used to judge a book's value and suitability for intended readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers list these details consistently; affordable price and adequate physical production influence accessibility and expected depth ('cheap, useful manuals' vs. risk of being 'too much cheapened').
